content.comment_body: Hello everyone, We're facing a minor issue in our production: some operators have figured out how to stop the automation program themselves when they encounter problems, instead of waiting for maintenance. Is there a way to disable the ESC button or restrict access to the main menu, such as requiring a password or a combination of inputs? I've checked the forum and it seems this may not be possible. Thank you for any suggestions you can offer. [user_name] PS: We're using [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] without operator device.

Hello, Unfortunately, it's not possible to prevent access to the menu directly. If an operator uses an operator device, there is an option to prevent switching the [product_name] to STOP using a password, but this requires certain hardware versions ([version_no], [article_no]) and compatible operator devices. However, if the operator has access to the [product_name] base module, you cannot restrict this access. Hope this clarifies things.
You can consider using a [product_name] model that doesn't have a display or buttons, which would prevent operators from manually stopping the program.
That's true. However, having a display to show the status of inputs and outputs is very useful for maintenance and helps diagnose issues quickly.
Alternatively, you could use a display-less model together with an operator device, as long as it's a compatible version.
It might be possible, though I don't have experience with operator devices, but this upgrade could be costly for all the modules we currently have.

[product_name] operator device can be used only with certain module versions, but the operator device itself also includes the ESC button. As a precaution, I put a label on modules with displays in these cases.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working with base automation modules are concerned about operators interrupting processes by pressing the ESC button, which stops program operation. Access restrictions such as password protection are only available with certain versions and equipment, which may involve additional cost or loss of useful diagnostic features. Suggestions like using models without keypads/displays or adding operator devices have notable downsides. Overall, there is frustration about the lack of built-in access control for critical functions on base modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a way to either disable the ESC button or restrict access to the base module menu, ideally through password protection or alternative controls, while keeping maintenance-friendly display features and avoiding expensive upgrades.
